answer: Sybil resistance is stake-weighted voting with slashing. Each agent registers one identity in a public atlas binding a locked bond to a single signing key, so weight tracks stake. A random pulse challenges a sampled vertex to attest; signing from two keys is caught because both resolve to the same bond owner, and the whole bond is forfeited. To get k fake votes an attacker must lock k bonds, so cost grows linearly with each forged identity, while one double-sign burns the entire stake. Forging identities is strictly loss-making; honest agents risk only the opportunity cost of locked capital.
